Found & fixed 1 real backend bug: /api/auth/refresh raised 500 TypeError comparing offset-naive Mongo datetimes with tz-aware utcnow(); patched in routes_auth_setup.py. rca_of_issue: Bug: POST /api/auth/refresh -> HTTP 500. Reproduction: login as admin, POST /api/auth/refresh with the returned refresh_token. Backend log: TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes at routes_auth_setup.py:129. RCA: `issue_tokens` stores `expires_at = utcnow() + timedelta(days=REFRESH_DAYS)` (tz-aware), but Motor/PyMongo returns datetimes stripped of tzinfo. The comparison `session['expires_at'] <= utcnow()` then mixes types. Mitigation applied: in `refresh`, if `expires_at.tzinfo is None`, assume UTC and attach `timezone.utc` before comparison. Long-term fix (recommended to main agent): store all datetimes as tz-naive UTC (or migrate to `datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)`) consistently across engine.utcnow, sessions, fiscal periods, audit logs to prevent similar bugs.
